_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for the Federated States of Micronesia covering Austronesian settlement (~2000 BCE), Nan Madol (megalithic city, Pohnpei, 'Venice of the Pacific'), Spanish colonisation (1886), German purchase (1899), Japanese mandate (1914-1945, Nanyo-cho), WWII (Chuuk/Truk Lagoon major Japanese naval base, air raids, Ghost Fleet), US Trust Territory (1947-1986), Compact of Free Association 1986, four-state federation (Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae).

country_profile.government_type: Federal presidential republic in free association with the United States

religion.note: Catholic dominant in Chuuk/Pohnpei/Yap (Spanish/German missionaries); Protestant in Kosrae (ABCFM missionaries, Congregational); Latter-day Saints; cultural Christianity blended with traditional beliefs; church central to island life; Sunday observance; parish structure mirrors colonial history

ethnic_groups.name: Chuukese
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest state by population (~48k); Austronesian; Chuuk Lagoon (former Truk, WWII Japanese naval base, 'Ghost Fleet' wreck diving); breadfruit culture; navigation traditions; outmigration to Guam/Hawaii/US mainland significant; inter-island tensions; sovereign state identity within federation

ethnic_groups.name: Pohnpeian
ethnic_groups.notes: Pohnpei Island (largest); Nan Madol (megalithic basalt city ~1200-1500 CE, 'Venice of the Pacific', UNESCO, one of most remarkable archaeological sites in Pacific); sakau/kava ceremony (central to social hierarchy); Saudeleur dynasty (legendary, built Nan Madol); federal capital Palikir located in Pohnpei

ethnic_groups.name: Kosraean
ethnic_groups.notes: Smallest state; Polynesian influences; Lelu Ruins (stone city, rival to Nan Madol); strongly Protestant/Congregational; conservative; 'Island of the Sleeping Lady' (mountain silhouette)

ethnic_groups.name: Yapese
ethnic_groups.notes: Unique culture; rai (stone money, massive limestone discs quarried from Palau, up to 4m diameter, value based on history not size, still used for traditional transactions, inspirational for blockchain/Bitcoin analogy); caste system; betel nut culture; traditional navigation (Carolinian stick charts, star paths); outer islands (Ulithi, Woleai, culturally distinct Carolinian navigators)

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Outer island Carolinians (Ulithian, Woleaian, Satawalese, master navigators, traditional canoe voyaging revived); Polynesian outliers (Nukuoro, Kapingamarangi); Filipino; American; Japanese (WWII legacy); significant diaspora in US (~40k COFA migrants, Guam/Hawaii/Arkansas/Oregon)

independence.from: US Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands (Compact of Free Association; US handles defence, citizens can live/work in US)

country_profile.notes_unique: Nan Madol (megalithic basalt city on Pohnpei, ~92 artificial islets on coral reef, built 1200-1500 CE by Saudeleur dynasty, 750k tons of basalt columns transported, 'Venice of the Pacific', UNESCO 2016, how stones moved remains mystery, spiritual centre of Pohnpei); Chuuk Lagoon/Ghost Fleet (Truk Lagoon, WWII Japanese naval base, Operation Hailstone Feb 1944 US air attack destroyed 12 warships/32 merchant ships/249 aircraft, now world's greatest wreck diving site, 60+ ships, oil still leaking environmental concern); Yapese stone money (rai, massive limestone discs quarried from Palau 400km away, transported by canoe, oral history records ownership, not physically moved when traded, parallels to modern cryptocurrency cited); Compact of Free Association (COFA, 1986 renewed 2023, US provides funding/defence, FSM citizens can live/work in US freely, ~40k in US, strategic denial of area to other powers, Pacific pivot importance); 607 islands across 2,700km of ocean (four states: Yap, Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae, extreme diversity, different languages, distinct cultures, fragile federation); traditional navigation (Carolinian navigators, star compass, wave reading, bird flight, no instruments, UNESCO, Mau Piailug taught Hawaiian canoe revival); betel nut (areca nut, universal social custom, red teeth); depopulation (emigration to US, brain drain, population declining); federation fragility (Chuuk secession discussions periodic); climate change (atolls vulnerable, sea level rise, freshwater lens contamination)
